conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Vestigia search 'Bonzagni': 46 items of Bonzagni's ASMo file; DECODE R1123/R1124/R1125 = b. 4 nos. 4, 6, 12 (Vestigia 1796, 1798, 1804).
Fetched the 11 DECODE images with the shared cookie.
Viewed every page: R1123 and R1124 carry contemporary interlinear decipherments over all cipher words; R1125 image 5 is a separate decipherment slip.

Aligned the slip ('Mando per Ladislao lator presto sei cavalli ...') with the first four lines of R1125's p. 3 cipher: word lengths agree and letters repeat consistently (sei, si, la, lator, poi, bacino, nove).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): entries with summaries for R1123, R1124 and R1125; no transcription and no decryption in the repository (the interlinear decipherments and the R1125 slip are on the DECODE images only; project work).

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): no text of R1123, R1124 or R1125 is in the repository (decode/*.htm are record pages; the decipherments are on the images only). All three relabelled decoded, not read; class already solved -> not read; method read from existing decipherment -> not solved, until the contemporary decipherments are transcribed.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b14): R1123-R1125 re-fetched from DECODE with the shared cookie (b14_fetch.py): page images only, no attachments or transcriptions; the Vestigia photographs (main checkout img/v/) are the same resolution.

R1125: the decipherment slip (image 5) transcribed and aligned group by group with the 12-line cipher block of p. 3: one slip word per group, letters repeating consistently; Latin-looking code words in the cipher found ('valent' = denaro, 'indigeo', 'parte' left blank by the slip) and a number .31. the slip omits.

R1124: the interlinear decipherment over the eight cipher lines transcribed and aligned with the cipher groups (texts/R1124_align.tsv); two more glossed cipher words in the clear text (tazze grande); the clear text of pp. 1-2 transcribed, with holes at the torn right edge.

R1123: the clear opening of p. 1, the first cipher block (ll. 5-9) and the start of the lower block transcribed from the glosses (texts/R1123_reading.md, partial); the gloss words checked against sign values from R1124/R1125 where legible (ducati, dona, del, fiorini, trecento, che). The rest of the lower block (an inventory of silver and sums, about eleven lines) and the cipher of p. 2 not finished: the brown gloss ink is faint at the scan's resolution, and the key was not rebuilt to decode the signs.

Clean-sentence share on the reading bodies: R1125 0.857, R1124 0.625 (inventory words outside the Italian lexicon), R1123 partial 0.632 on the part read. R1124 and R1125 set read; R1123 kept decoded, not read (most of its cipher unread).

outcome.method_basis: R1124 and R1125 read from the contemporary decipherments (the interlinear glosses of R1124, the decipherment slip of R1125), transcribed and aligned with the cipher groups on 22 Oct 2026; R1123's glosses only partly transcribed.
outcome.notes: Read at the time. Added here only the check that the R1125 slip is the decipherment of its cipher block. Catalogue entry 155 removed; no write-up. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: none of the three decipherments is transcribed here; all three entries decoded, not read; class already solved -> not read, method -> not solved until they are transcribed. 22 Oct 2026, re-read (b14): R1125's slip and R1124's glosses transcribed and aligned with the cipher; both read (texts/). R1123 read in part (p. 1 upper block); its lower block and p. 2 stay open. The cipher carries Latin-looking code words (potest = Re d'Ungaria, valent = denaro/argenti, indigeo, parte).

credits.note: interlinear decipherments on R1123, R1124 and the decipherment slip filed with R1125

texts.label: Eger, 2 Aug 1512
texts.summary: Giovanni Battista Bonzagni, Ippolito I d'Este's agent at Eger, writes to the cardinal; the political news (Bakócz, the Tatar khan, Poland, the Diet) is in clear, and the c. 14 cipher lines on p. 1 cover private and household business, the estate of a dead man's goods and jewels.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (b14), partial: texts/R1123_reading.md and _en.md hold the clear opening of p. 1, the first cipher block (ll. 5-9, from the gloss: a thousand gold ducats gathered, the King of Hungary's order that the troops ride out by the August feast of Our Lady, 300 florins through Alberto Pratonerio's father) and the start of the lower block (madonna Beatrice's estate, sums in florins). Not read: the rest of the lower block of p. 1 (about eleven glossed lines, an inventory of silver and sums) and the glossed cipher of p. 2 (ll. 2-4, 7). Blockers: illegible (the brown gloss ink is faint at the resolution of the DECODE and Vestigia photographs) and not-attempted (a key rebuilt from the R1124/R1125 alignments would decode the signs and settle the faint glosses).

texts.label: Eger, 4 Aug 1512
texts.summary: Bonzagni to Ippolito I d'Este: eight cipher lines on Beatrice's jewels (cups, bowls, salts).

reading_review.note: Read 22 Oct 2026 (b14): the eight cipher lines from the contemporary interlinear decipherment, transcribed from the DECODE image and aligned group by group with the cipher (texts/R1124_align.tsv), with the clear text of pp. 1-2 transcribed around them; _check_reading.py on the body 0.625 (20/32; misses mostly inventory words the Italian lexicon lacks: coppa, tazette, anelle, coramo). Holes: the torn right edge of p. 1 (ll. 12-19) and the end of cipher l. 5.

texts.label: Eger, 28 Dec 1514
texts.summary: Bonzagni to Ippolito I d'Este: the 13-line cipher block on p. 3 says he is sending six horses by Ladislao with a list, a silver basin and a bronzina, and cannot send money; the clear p. 4 continues the same business.

reading_review.note: Read 22 Oct 2026 (b14): the 12-line cipher block of p. 3 from the decipherment slip filed with the letter (image 5), transcribed and aligned group by group with the cipher (texts/R1125_align.tsv); _check_reading.py on the body 0.857 (6/7). Open: the code word 'parte' (left blank by the slip) and the number .31.; the clear pp. 1-4 not transcribed here.

gaps.item: R1123: the lower cipher block of p. 1 (about eleven glossed lines, an inventory of silver and sums) and the glossed cipher of p. 2 (ll. 2-4, 7)
gaps.detail: the brown gloss ink is faint at the resolution of the DECODE and Vestigia photographs (both c. 3000 px for the whole sheet); partly legible words: coppe, dorate, tondi dodici, pesano, marche, oncie cinque, pesetti due

gaps.item: R1123: key rebuild to decode the signs under the faint glosses
gaps.detail: a substitution of invented signs with homophones for vowels and a few Latin-looking code words; R1124 and R1125 (texts/*_align.tsv) give about 170 aligned words to rebuild it from; then decode R1123's lower block and p. 2 and check the glosses

gaps.item: R1125: the code word 'parte' (cipher l. 7) and the number .31. (l. 10)
gaps.detail: the slip leaves the first blank and omits the second; seen once

gaps.item: R1124: the torn right edge of p. 1 (ll. 12-19 of the clear text) and the end of cipher l. 5
